title: On-call buddy system and micro-retrospective playbook
author: Priya Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines an operational pattern we adopted at Redwood to reduce responder fatigue, accelerate effective incident handoffs, and capture higher-fidelity evidence for post-incident learning. It combines a lightweight on-call buddy system with a disciplined micro-retrospective loop that runs immediately after shifts and after major incidents. The document includes checklist-driven runbook excerpts, automation recommendations, and canonical status/csr templates for customer-facing communication.

Scope:

- Applies to on-call engineers and bridge operators supporting Redwood inference runtime, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments.
- Intended for rotations with single primary and secondary (buddy) model.
- Integrates with existing runbooks, SLA/credit policies, and postmortem processes; it does not replace full postmortems for Sev1 incidents.

Goals and non-goals:

- Goals:
  - Reduce single-person decision bottlenecks during noisy degradation windows.
  - Capture evidence and customer impact artifacts at time-of-event (not only during postmortem).
  - Create a low-friction path to psychological safety and learning for junior responders.
- Non-goals:
  - This is not a replacement for full incident reviews or for escalation matrices.

Definitions and roles:

- Primary responder: the person paged and responsible for first-triage and immediate mitigation steps.
- Buddy (secondary): assigned at the beginning of a shift; remains available for consultation, takeover, or to coordinate cross-team comms.
- Bridge operator: runs the incident bridge if activated; may be the Primary or Buddy depending on severity.
- Incident steward: assigned for Sev1/2 incidents to coordinate evidence capture and postmortem artifacts after initial stabilization.

On-call buddy system (operational pattern):

1) Shift start (5-minute ritual):
   - Primary posts availability in #oncall-status with name, buddy name, and a short note: current capacity (full/limited), any planned offline windows.
   - Buddy confirms by replying and declaring explicit overlap windows if any.

2) Buddy responsibilities while on-call:
   - Be reachable and respond within 10 minutes for escalations from Primary during working hours (Slack/phone policy).
   - Offer immediate validation for high impact remediation (e.g., rolling restarts, model rollbacks).
   - Take over bridge operations if the Primary must step away or is overwhelmed.
   - Kick off containment actions if cascading failures are observed and Primary is blocked.

3) Handoffs and shadowing:
   - If Primary must hand off mid-incident, Buddy performs a rapid 3-point verbal handover: summary, actions taken, next critical step. Document handover in the incident channel.

4) Escalation etiquette:
   - For latency SLO breaches > 4% sustained for 5 minutes, escalate to SRE lead and the oncall-ops windowing policy triggers. Buddy should coordinate immediate mitigation step (scale/route/fallback).

Micro-retrospective loop (post-shift or post-incident, lightweight):

Purpose: capture the signal while fresh, identify one to two action items, maintain psychological safety.

When to run:
- After any page that required > 15 minutes of active intervention (even if resolved).
- At the end of each shift if the Primary responded to any page.

Format (10–20 minutes):
1. Data snapshot (2–3 min): Primary summarizes the incident timeline and outcome.
2. What worked / what didn’t (5–7 min): concise bullets (no finger-pointing).
3. Action items (3–5 min): 1–2 owners, small scope, target date.
4. Knowledge capture (2–3 min): add a 3-line runbook excerpt or update existing runbook.

Example micro-retro entry template (use in Slack or incident tracker):
- Incident: KV cache eviction spike causing 30% latency increase (2026-02-18 03:12 UTC)
- Primary: Jordan Lee, Buddy: Priya Patel
- Outcome: Increased replicas for ranking-service, restored to 95th percentile target in 7m
- Action items:
  - Add an automatic throttle rule for spiky traffic (owner: S. Ramirez, due: 2026-03-07)
  - Update ranking-service runbook to include cache-eviction indicators (owner: J. Lee, due: 2026-03-01)

Automations and tooling (recommended integrations):

- Slack slash command: /oncall-buddy start <buddy> that writes a JSON record to the incident-tracker with start time and members. Example payload saved automatically to the tracker.
- Post-incident: a GitHub issue template auto-created with micro-retro content when incident severity >= 2. Fields: timeline, immediate mitigations, evidence artifacts, action items.
- Evidence capture hook: when a bridge is opened, the bridge bot snapshots the last 30 minutes of traces, the current SLO dashboard, and pinned logs to the incident artifacts bucket.

Runbook excerpt: brief example for latency spike affecting hosted API (copy into the appropriate service runbook).

1) Confirm impact:
   - Check dashboards: api-latency-95, kv-cache-hit-rate, model-serving-qps
   - run: curl -sS https://status.internal/api/health | jq .latency_p95
2) Quick containment (first 5 minutes):
   - If kv-cache-hit-rate < 60%: temporarily increase replica count: kubectl scale deployment/model-serving --replicas=6 -n prod
   - If model-serving CPU > 85% and latency at p95 > 2s: switch traffic to model-variant-b: apply routing patch
3) Evidence collection (immediate):
   - Run: ./tools/collect-incident-evidence --since=30m --service=model-serving --out=/tmp/incident-ARTIFACTS.tar.gz
   - Post artifacts to incident tracker and tag in bridge: /attach /tmp/incident-ARTIFACTS.tar.gz

Status page and customer comm templates (canonical):

- Short public status entry (for service-impacting latency events):
  Title: "Reduced response performance for Redwood API (partial impact)"
  Body: "We are investigating elevated response times for a subset of API requests affecting some customers in US-West. Engineers are actively investigating. We will update within 30 minutes."
  Visibility: public

- Escalated public status entry (if > 30 minutes and customer impact persists):
  Title: "Ongoing degradation of API performance — mitigation in progress"
  Body: "We are seeing persistent elevated latency for some models in US-West. We have increased capacity and are validating traffic routing changes. If you are experiencing issues, please contact support@redwood.ai with your request id and affected region. Estimated next update: 30 minutes."
  Visibility: public

- Private customer notice template (for affected Enterprise customers):
  Subject: "Redwood incident: degraded API latency impacting [customer-name] — interim remediation applied"
  Body:
  "Hi [Customer Name],

  We wanted to notify you that we observed elevated API latency for requests to models hosted in US-West beginning at 2026-02-18 02:48 UTC. Our on-call team has applied a targeted capacity increase and validated traffic routing; service is performing within acceptable bounds for most traffic.

  What we did: increased serving replicas, applied routing patch to divert traffic from impacted model variants, collected artifacts for deeper analysis.

  Next steps: we will confirm root cause and share a timeline for a permanent fix in the post-incident report. Estimated time for next update: 2 hours.

  Contact: [Account Manager], [Support Contact], incident ID: INC-20260218-317

  Thanks,
  Redwood Incident Response
  "

Game day integration (how to validate the pattern):

- Scenario: sustained kv-cache eviction spike that causes p95 latency to exceed SLO for 10 minutes.
- Objectives:
  - Validate buddy takeover behavior when Primary needs to step away.
  - Ensure micro-retro templates are auto-created and small action items are tracked to closure.
  - Verify evidence snapshot hook captures correct artifacts (traces + SLO dashboard charts).
- Metrics to capture during the exercise:
  - Mean time to first mitigation (target < 7 minutes)
  - Time to buddy acknowledgment (target < 10 minutes)
  - % of micro-retro action items created during shift that are closed within 14 days (target >= 70%)

Operational thresholds and SLOs referenced:

- API p95 latency SLO: 1.2s (global), error budget window: 30 days
- KV cache hit-rate healthy threshold: >= 75%
- On-call acknowledgement target: 1 minute for primary, 10 minutes for buddy during working hours

Escalation and evidence policy (brief):

- For any incident that meets Sev1 criteria (customer outage or regulatory impact), Incident Steward must run the evidence collection hook and ensure artifacts are uploaded to the secure evidence bucket before the postmortem kickoff.
- For Sev2 incidents captured by micro-retro, the steward may delegate artifact capture to the Buddy if the Primary is occupied.

Ownership, rollout, and training:

- Pilot: start with SRE and Serving Runtime teams for a six-week pilot.
- Measurement: weekly adoption report produced by rota-bot showing buddy confirmations, micro-retros submitted, and action item closure rate.
- Training: 90-minute workshop + 2 game days to practice buddy takeover and micro-retro execution.
- Owner: Priya Patel (Oncall Experience), Ops training assigned to Ethan Chen.

Appendix: quick commands and templates

- Start buddy command (example):
  - /oncall-buddy start @Priya --shift=2026-03-01T09:00Z
- Evidence collection (local):
  - ./tools/collect-incident-evidence --service=ranking-service --since=15m --out=./incident-1234.tar.gz
- Micro-retro quick checklist (copy to incident channel):
  1) Timeline + outcome
  2) 1 thing that went well
  3) 1 improvement item (owner + due date)
  4) Paste evidence artifact link

Appendix B: Measurement dashboard (fields to include)

- Buddy confirmation rate (percent of shifts where buddy acknowledged within 10 minutes)
- Micro-retro submission rate (percent of pages with a micro-retro added within 24 hours)
- Action item closure rate within 14 days
- Average evidence-upload time from bridge open
